title: C-zero stability of visible length spectral values within primitive flat knot types on closed Riemannian surfaces
source_title: From curve shortening to flat link stability and Birkhoff sections of geodesic flows
author: Marcelo R. R. Alves; Marco Mazzucchelli
difficulty_reason: A small C-zero metric perturbation controls loop lengths and subloop areas but does not control the curve-shortening vector field in the stronger topology normally used for continuation. The authors construct a new two-parameter interleaving inside the fixed primitive knot type, selecting six length levels and five exit thresholds around a visible spectral gap. Their complete diagram preserves the obstruction to a homotopy equivalence for the perturbed metric without assuming isolated or non-degenerate geodesics.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem4.2: closed Riemannian surface (M,g), primitive flat knot type K, visible spectral value ell in sigma_g^v(K) as defined in Section4.1. Every sufficiently C-zero-close Riemannian metric h has a visible spectral value in any prescribed interval (ell-epsilon,ell+epsilon). No orientability, non-degeneracy or isolated-geodesic condition is added to this exact theorem. Full new interleaving proof28–29 read: close metrics control both length and subloop areas; the six-level inclusion diagram and homotopy equivalences imply persistence of a visible h-spectrum value. The primitive flat-knot/exit-set constructions9–11 are explicitly traced to Angenent2005 Lemmas3.3/5.3–4/6.2/6.3/6.6 and Proposition6.8, with classical curve-shortening existence/compactness background. Section3 intro18 provides spectrum closedness and Sard measure-zero property; exact definition of visibility28 included. The terminal sigma_h^v(Sigma) display uses Sigma where all definitions and the full authored argument refer to K; this unambiguous notation typo is retained unchanged without an assistant mathematical repair. No full-link intertwining theorem4.5 or forced/Birkhoff existence outcome is counted. Those distinct outcomes are not certified by this selection; the reviewed source includes nearby30–35 only as context, and the chosen primary proof does not depend on their stopped-flow displays. Whole52-page original retained with original2025volume12 publication and acquisition dates.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors combine the singular curve-shortening semiflow and metric-independent exit sets with a metric interleaving of length and subloop-area filtrations to preserve homotopically visible spectral values under only continuous metric perturbations. This infinite-dimensional geometric Conley argument exceeds ordinary qualifying examinations.
